title: Tech Support Is Sales: Turning support into your brand, sales channel and product research
summary: Jason Cohen argues tech support is the face of your company and often the only human contact customers have with you. At Smart Bear, great support closed individual and six-figure enterprise deals without a traditional sales team, and doubled as the closest thing to customer development for a bootstrapper.

principles.text: For most customers, tech support is the only human interaction they have with your company, so staffing it with your worst-treated, least-qualified people is a mistake.
principles.quote: For most of your customers, **tech support is the only human interaction they'll have with you.** Are you really going to leave that up to your worst-treated, least-paid, least-qualified employees?

principles.text: You can win large deals without a classic sales team if your support genuinely makes customers successful.
principles.quote: At Smart Bear we made millions of dollars in both individual and enterprise sales without "sales."

principles.text: The purpose of support is to make customers fantastic at their jobs, not just to answer their literal question. Find out what they are trying to accomplish and help with that.
principles.quote: I say **the purpose of tech support is to make your customers fantastic at their jobs**, which happen to involve your product.

principles.text: Make the customer awesome and she will pay you so she can keep being awesome. Enablement is a whole-company job, not only a product feature.
principles.quote: Make your customer awesome and she'll give you money so she can keep being awesome.

principles.text: Because customers expect bad support, simply acting human (a non-automated email reply) earns outsized goodwill and word of mouth.
principles.quote: When your customers expect a turd sandwich and you deliver a turkey club with chipotle aioli, you earn major bonus points

principles.text: Mine support conversations for the meta-questions behind each problem: confusion, terminology, mismatched worldview, and unmet needs that point to new products or pivots. This is how Smart Bear found code review.
principles.quote: This last line of questioning is exactly [how Smart Bear came to be](https://longform.asmartbear.com/product-market-fit-formula/) a company about peer code review and not "version control data mining."
